endings.label: Spending the Rest of Life: Little Sister
endings.description:
My dear friend:
The war is over; the smoke of battle has long since cleared. Only now do I dare to take up my pen and write to you. The reason, as you well know, is that I ultimately chose not to press forward—at the very moment when all others were rushing toward the final reckoning, toward glory and sacrifice, I stopped, turned, and walked away.
Is this cowardice? I deserted on the greater path. Though I have regained the power to steer my own life, the war has left its marks upon me—they are like scars on the soul, so that I often cannot tell where the snows of the Volga end and where the perpetual chill lodged in my bones begins. I think that part of me which I left behind on the battlefield will forever resent itself, until I die, until I truly die.
But I will say this: for one living being I was willing to cease all killing, and I have never regretted that halt. Because of her love, because of my love, because perhaps she alone bears me no resentment—and the door she opened for me is greater, to me, than every door in the Mansus. You know that someone once said: scars are doors of pain and possibility. It was she who led me through that door, and perhaps one day everyone will pass through it under Janus's gaze, treading in our footsteps, toward the future we together hope for. It is said that the Twins have not yet been struck from the rolls after the war—this is good. It suggests that love does indeed triumph over pain, and even over the Corner-Crawl.
Look—she is calling me. I must lay down my pen.

Yours,
—From a letter to 'the Exile', Crimea, 1945

endings.label: The Inevitable Path
endings.description:
Passing through the Stag Door, all that was mortal is extinguished. The Colonel names me in the smoke of war. Henceforth I am a piece on his unfolded battle map; in the assaults that no staff officer can explain, there lies the trace of my existence. The other Named Ones gather round and salute me in silence. We each fulfill our roles, taking ever more resolute strides toward our common goal.
I have discovered another grid on the battle map – that is the domain of another god, and the path to the door of victory lies within it. Among the scale-like color patches that all my marching arrows toward victory must rely on, I see her figure. My beloved. So her undulations aid my advance, and my victory becomes her extension.
I am war. She is the road. War is never achieved by one person alone, and a road is never trod by one alone.

[Congratulations on achieving one of the great victory endings. Even a minor victory might be achieved by only one in twenty players – and those who ascend this far are even fewer. We, and Janus, salute you.]

endings.label: Two-legged Worm
endings.description: Now, at last, I realize I know nothing of the Mansus. I am certain I am disconnected from reality; I am now at the center of a great sea, though I have never seen the sea in my life. “Mother Mokosh, I have lost my way, the path ahead is hidden. Show me the trail, lest I perish in this wilderness.” (Мати Мокошь, аз неведєнь, путь сокрытъ. Укажи ми стєзю, да не погинє во пустыни.)
